results.title: A — acquire + hold standing (support: candidate)
results.note: Starts in Gate A's relaxed drop-A pose resting on the turf; at t = 0 the motors switch on with the neutral-stance target (a step request). Finite motors must bring the body into the stance and hold it.

results.title: A — acquire + hold standing (support: REDUCED ×0.25)
results.note: Same as A with the temporary pelvis support at a quarter strength.

results.title: A — acquire + hold standing (support: OFF)
results.note: Same as A with NO pelvis support: only the joint motors, the feet on the turf and friction.

results.title: B — slow transition: stance → knee raise → stance (1.5 s each)
results.note: Right hip + knee flex, trunk leans, arms counter-swing; the stance foot and the COM target stay over the left foot.

results.title: B — slow transition (support: REDUCED ×0.25)
results.note: B with a quarter-strength pelvis support.

results.title: B — slow transition (support: OFF)
results.note: B with no pelvis support: single-leg stance with no balance controller.

results.title: C — fast transition (0.3 s) — CANDIDATE strength
results.note: The same poses as B, five times faster: expect tracking lag and saturation, not unlimited force.

results.title: C — fast transition — TOO WEAK (×0.25 authority + stiffness)
results.note: Strength comparison: the same request with a quarter of the torque limits and stiffness.

results.title: C — fast transition — TOO STRONG (×8 authority + stiffness)
results.note: Strength comparison: eight times the torque limits and stiffness.

results.title: D1 — target REVERSAL mid-motion
results.note: The fast knee raise starts (0.35 s min-jerk); at 0.65 s, near peak target velocity, the request reverses and returns linearly to the stance in 0.3 s.

results.title: D2 — target STEP CHANGE mid-motion
results.note: The fast knee raise starts; at 0.70 s the request jumps instantly to a back-swing pose (hip extension, deep knee flexion, arms swapped), held 1 s, then back to the stance.

results.title: E — BLOCKED LIMB: leg reach through a fixed post, post removed at 3.0 s
results.note: The right leg is asked to swing forward to a 60° hip flexion; a fixed, immovable post (r 5.5 cm, a shin-sized obstacle) sits in its path. At 3.0 s the post is removed from the world.

results.title: E — blocked limb — TOO STRONG (×8)
results.note: The fixed post against eight times the motor authority: contact must still win.

results.title: E — movable post — TOO WEAK (×0.25)
results.note: The post is movable: 25 kg on a finite spring (2500 N/m, force limit 180 N per axis) — a finite-strength obstacle.

results.title: E — movable post — CANDIDATE
results.note: The movable finite-strength post against the candidate motors.

results.title: E — movable post — TOO STRONG (×8): bulldozing
results.note: The movable post against eight times the motor authority.

results.title: F — disturbance: shove at the right shoulder
results.note: Holding the stance; at 1.0 s a 50 ms impulse of 47 N·s (≈ a firm shove) acts on the chest at the right shoulder, toward his left and slightly back.

results.title: F — shove at the right shoulder (support: OFF)
results.note: F_chest with no pelvis support: only the joint motors resist; there is no balance controller.

results.title: F — disturbance: shove at the pelvis
results.note: Holding the stance; at 1.0 s a 50 ms impulse of 45 N·s acts on the pelvis, backward.

results.title: F — disturbance: knock on the left hand
results.note: Holding the stance; at 1.0 s a 50 ms impulse of 7 N·s acts on the left hand, upward and forward.
